headline: The US is delaying the transfer of 60 Patriot missiles to Ukraine. Kyiv was due to receive 8 PAC-3 missiles in September, 10 in October, another 10 in November and 12 in December. The transfer of an additional 20 PAC-2 missiles also requires Pentagon approval, despite the deliveries being funded by European countries. Dang, that's extremely low. The US has its own stockpile shortages to deal with, and although it's trying to ramp up production, that will take time. I think Ukraine would be much better off relying more on European alternatives that it already operates, such as IRIS-T SLM and SAMP/T, rather than waiting for just 10 PAC-3 missiles a month. Those could be used up in a single hour during a major Russian missile attack. At some point, you have to accept that Iskander-Ms will get through and save the interceptors for other incoming threats.

headline: Footage released by the Security Service of Ukraine (SBU) shows Ukrainian unmanned surface vessel (USV) attacks on the Russian Navy's Project 20380 corvette Mercury (734), which was docked at the Libyan port of Benghazi, and the Ro-Ro cargo ship ASCALON off the coast of Benghazi. During the attack on the corvette, one USV struck the vessel, followed by a second USV that detonated inside the resulting breach. A third USV also struck the starboard side, away from the initial breach. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy also claimed that a Ka-27 helicopter was destroyed. However, this claim cannot be verified, as no helicopter is visible aboard the corvette in the released footage. The footage also shows projectiles flying past one of the USVs as Russian forces attempt to repel the attack. During a second attack in broad daylight, a Ukrainian USV struck the Russian Ro-Ro cargo ship ASCALON. However, Zelenskyy's claim that the vessel hit was the Russian cargo ship ANGARA appears to be incorrect. Footage released by the Libyan Arab Armed Forces (LAAF), included in this video, shows the ASCALON being struck. Also, the ANGARA was last spotted five days ago near Madagascar, heading towards the Seychelles.
summary: Footage released by the Security Service of Ukraine (SBU) shows Ukrainian unmanned surface vessel (USV) attacks on the Russian Navy's Project 20380 corvette Mercury (734), which was docked at the Libyan port of Benghazi, and the Ro-Ro cargo ship ASCALON off the coast of Benghazi.

headline: The Pentagon has not approved the transfer of about 60 Patriot interceptors the U.S. had agreed to supply to Ukraine, according to the Financial Times, citing two Ukrainian officials and a third person familiar with the matter. The sources say Secretary of War Pete Hegseth has delayed the shipments. The missiles, including some in European arsenals and paid for by Kyiv's allies, need U.S. approval to be exported or re-exported. The transfers include some 40 PAC-3 interceptors, Ukraine's most effective defense against Russian ballistic missiles, scheduled for delivery between September and December, and about 20 older PAC-2s. None of the four PAC-3 shipments have been approved. A Pentagon spokesperson told the FT there has been no change to policy on support for Ukraine and declined further questions. Zelenskyy has said Ukraine received an average of 12 U.S. Patriot interceptors a month this year, while Russia fires about 150 ballistic missiles a month. He warned Monday that Ukrainian intelligence indicates Russia is preparing new strikes.

headline: The 8th Circuit Court of Appeals has denied the emergency stay request and lifted its administrative stay of the permit from the Environmental Protection Agency, clearing the way for the U.S. Army's controlled detonation of 68 barrels containing a 9,773lbs of degraded lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant, near Middletown. The court found the permit's safeguards adequate. They include containment barriers, weather restrictions, public notification, and lead sampling and cleanup requirements. Both sides agreed the detonation will cause some public harm. The court said the real choice was between a controlled detonation with mitigation in place and an uncontrolled explosion with none. The Army had said it intends to act by November 25th.

headline: An oil tanker exploded and caught fire after hitting a sea mine east of the Strait of Hormuz at dawn, the IRGC Navy claimed. According to the IRGC, the vessel was sailing an unauthorized route through the strait. Two other tankers traveling with it turned back to the Persian Gulf after seeing the blast and receiving a radio warning from the IRGC Navy. Iranian outlet Fararu described it as the fourth tanker explosion east of the strait.

headline: Per Reuters, a U.S. Senate panel is investigating Vice President JD Vance over Vitol's Venezuelan oil deal. The question: whether Vance helped the commodities giant secure it. Vitol and rival Trafigura have since made hundreds of millions of dollars selling Venezuelan oil. Vance allegedly met Vitol trader John Addison shortly before the U.S. invasion of Venezuela in January. Both deny the meeting took place. Addison gave $300,000 to support Vance's 2022 Senate campaign. He and his wife also gave $7 million to support Trump's 2024 election bid.

headline: German police assess the bomb threats sent to more than 450 schools on November 23 as hoaxes with no concrete danger. Schools were told to continue normal operations. The identical emails were signed "Allahu Akbar." Subject line: "Death awaits you" (Der Tod erwartet dich). They claimed ammonium nitrate and nitromethane explosives were placed in schools. They also demanded the government resign and called for Sharia law. Similar threats reached schools in Denmark.
